text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — PD-INC-9241 — gpu-rack-23-node-7 reported KERNEL_OOPS and kubelet NotReady. Autopage to eng-oncall. Host offline from heartbeat.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-9241 assigned to Maya Patel (acknowledged). Escalation timer paused.

Maya Patel: ack, I'm on it. Starting collection. @Ajay can you grab serial console if I need it? I'll query kube state.

Ajay Singh: on call standby. If you need serial, I'll attach. FYI I just saw similar oops earlier on rack-21 — might be kernel bug recurring.

Maya Patel: running quick checks:
```
kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-rack-23-node-7
# output: gpu-rack-23-node-7   NotReady   <none>   12m
kubectl describe node gpu-rack-23-node-7
# kubelet lastHeartbeat: 2024-05-07T15:34:21Z
# Events: Kernel panic message (dmesg) referenced in node-exporter logs
```

Lee Park: pinging rack telemetry, nvme/dmesg collectors.

incident-bot: telemetry-scan started for host gpu-rack-23-node-7. Artifacts: /artifacts/PD-9241/3418209999.tar.gz

Maya Patel: Checking pods on that node via scheduler API to determine customer impact.
```
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-rack-23-node-7 -o wide
# 8 pods found: 3 tenant-prod, 4 infra (runtime), 1 batch-job
```

Toni Ramos: Which tenants? Any SLA owners alerted? I'll start customer notifications if prod impact > 1 tenant.

Maya Patel: tenants: tenant-alpha, tenant-kite, tenant-solaris. tenant-alpha has 2 model endpoints. Failover policy should route to spare nodes but we need to confirm capacity.

Ajay Singh: Initiating drain check -> will attempt cordon + drain if kubelet responsive. If it's NotReady and unreachable, we may need force-evict and failover.

Maya Patel: Trying cordon:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-rack-23-node-7
# Warning: node gpu-rack-23-node-7 not found or control-plane unable to reach kubelet
```

Lee Park: Serial shows host kernel oops at timestamp, followed by watchdog reset. Looks like kernel panic loop. NIC & NVMe flapping seen. Host not answering SSH.

pagerduty-bot: PD escalation policy will escalate to SRE lead in 10m if no resolution.

Toni Ramos: Customer impact summary for ops notes:
- 3 tenant endpoints had pods on the host
- Immediate effect: endpoints for tenant-alpha returned 503 for ~30s during failover
- No broader region outage detected

Maya Patel: Good. I will trigger evacuation of pods from scheduler side and mark host as unschedulable in inventory. Steps:
1) Mark host OutOfService in infra inventory
2) Kick RMA workflow if hardware fault
3) Reroute inference traffic if canary sees degradation

Ajay Singh: I have serial access and will attempt IPMI reboot once we have artifacts pulled. Collecting coredumps now via iDRAC -> pushing to /artifacts/PD-9241/coredump.

incident-bot: artifact upload complete: /artifacts/PD-9241/{dmesg,syslog,coredump}. Tarball size 120MB.

Maya Patel: Because kubelet is NotReady and host is flapping, I'm triggering a logical evacuation for tenant pods so they can be rescheduled: `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0 --namespace tenant-alpha <pod>` for the 2 critical endpoints, and similarly for tenant-kite. Not ideal but necessary.

Lee Park: Noted. I'll monitor cluster autoscaler; might need to spin spare GPU capacity for tenant-solaris batch-job.

Toni Ramos: I sent initial notification to affected customers: "We detected a host failure impacting a subset of model endpoints; engineers are responding and failover is in progress. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA." Response: tenant-alpha reported transient errors but back to normal after failover.

Maya Patel: Update: forced deletion succeeded; pods coming up on other nodes. No increased error budget for tenants based on short window. Marking incident as partial customer impact.

pagerduty-bot: Maya Patel marked PD-INC-9241 as under investigation. Next SLA checkpoint in 30m.

Ajay Singh: IPMI reboot attempted: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.23.5.7 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle` -> host didn't respond to IPMI; suspect BMC flapping. Raising RMA.

Lee Park: NVMe SMART shows multiple media errors. Likely hardware fault causing kernel panic via driver interaction.

Maya Patel: Action list for postmortem:
- RMA gpu-rack-23-node-7 (BMC + NVMe) — Ajay
- Collect full metrics 1h pre/post (Lee)
- Confirm scheduler reschedule behavior and fast-fail thresholds (Maya)
- Add runbook step: prefer graceful pod evacuation fallback when kubelet unreachable (Toni)

Toni Ramos: I'll open customer follow-up with timeline & mitigations. Also adding a note to runbook to include detection of repeated kernel oops pattern and auto-quarantine host earlier.

oncall-rotation-bot: rotating next oncall is Lee Park at 2024-05-07T17:00Z — handoff prep recommended.

Maya Patel: Handing off active investigation to Lee for long-running RMA and telemetry deep-dive. Leaving priority actions in ticket PD-9241. @Lee you have the artifacts and RMA authority.

Lee Park: Taking over. I'll coordinate with hardware support and update PD ticket. ETA for hardware RMA initial response: 2h.

Maya Patel: Thanks team — closing Slack thread for live coordination. I'll post a short incident summary in #incidents once RMA confirmed. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PD-INC-9241 updated: Owner changed to Lee Park. Thread closed for real-time ops; monitoring continues.
